speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and does the pain worsen after you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your 5-month history of bladder discomfort relieved by voiding, frequency, and dyspareunia, I need to rule out a urinary tract infection or interstitial cystitis. Have you noticed any visible blood in your urine, or have you been diagnosed with a sexually transmitted infection recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming. To further narrow the differential between interstitial cystitis and a pelvic floor disorder, do you experience significant pain or tightness when I perform a digital rectal exam or internal pelvic exam? Also, have you noticed any changes in the appearance or odor of your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS). Given the 5-month history of bladder pain relieved by voiding, urinary frequency, dyspareunia, and the absence of pyuria or infection, the clinical picture strongly supports IC/BPS, likely exacerbated by lithium use. No further tests are needed at this time.
